summary:
São Paulo State University (Unesp) is a public university funded by the state of São Paulo. Founded in 1976 by bringing together independent public colleges, it now has 23 campuses and 33 teaching, research and extension units, with more than 45,000 students. Its oldest institution, the Araraquara Pharmacy and Odontology Faculty, dates to 1923.

Unesp’s facilities include 30 libraries holding about 900,000 books, 1,900 laboratories, two hospitals with roughly 800 beds, veterinary hospitals and clinics, and five experimental farms. Its 2015 budget was R$2.6 billion. A rector, appointed by the state governor from three candidates chosen in university elections, leads the institution; a University Council makes major decisions.

The university employs about 3,500 teachers and 10,600 other staff. It offers 171 undergraduate options and 118 postgraduate programs, serving around 10,000 postgraduate students. Admission is through a competitive two-stage exam; some arts, design and architecture courses require additional tests.

Unesp has 140 international exchange and cooperation agreements across 52 countries. Since 2013, its International Courses program has covered agricultural sciences, alternative energy, dentistry, and literature and linguistics.

Rankings cited in the article place Unesp among Brazil’s leading universities and Latin America’s top institutions. In 2017, ARWU placed it in the world’s 301–400 group and third in Brazil; THE placed it in the 601–800 group in 2018. UNESCO reported in 2010 that Unesp produced 8% of Brazil’s scientific output at international level, second nationally alongside Unicamp and behind USP. Its research focuses include bioenergy, biotechnology, climate change, nanotechnology, health, public policy, marine science and stem cells.

Notable alumni include television presenter Ana Maria Braga, singer Bruna Caram, sociologist Heleieth Saffioti and composer Edson Zampronha. The university is Brazil’s only member of the Compostela Group of Universities.
